Find the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
after.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $m∠A={45}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AB}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({45}^{∘}) & =\frac{x+3}{2x} \\ 1 & =\frac{x+3}{2x} \\ 2x & =x+3 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =x+3=3+3=6, \\ AB & =2x=2(3)=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 6 \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $m∠C={30}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠C,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AB}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠C) & =\frac{AB}{BC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘}) & =\frac{\sqrt{3}(x-1)}{2x+1} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}(x-1)}{2x+1} \\ \sqrt{3}(2x+1) & =3\sqrt{3}(x-1) \\ 2x+1 & =3x-3 \\ x & =4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\sqrt{3}(x-1)=\sqrt{3}(4-1)=3\sqrt{3}, \\ BC & =2x+1=2(4)+1=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\sqrt{3}\cdot 9 \\  & =\frac{27\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
